summary: The generated build.fsx Run target stalls indefinitely because runProcess reads redirected pipes to EOF, and MSBuild worker nodes spawned as children of dotnet run outlive it holding the inherited write handles.
evidence: command:./fake.sh build -t Run (no stdout, killed at 300s, exit 124); file:build.fsx; proc:/proc/<msbuild-node>/fd/1 resolved to the same pipe the finished dotnet run had been given; issue:EHotwagner/rogue3#14
cost: 6+ minutes of silent stall per invocation; the target was unusable and docs/product.md already carries a setsid backgrounding workaround instead
owner: FS.GG.UI scaffold template — the generated build.fsx runProcess helper, which every generated product inherits

summary: GovernanceTests pins five literal strings from inside runProcess's body, so repairing the deadlock had to preserve the exact expression that caused it and route the new diagnostic through the stderr binding to keep 'let output = stdout + stderr' verbatim.
cost: one design iteration abandoned: a bounded ReadToEndAsync drain satisfied the pins but discarded all captured output, proven by a harness returning stdout=0 chars; replaced with incremental collection
owner: FS.GG.UI scaffold template — governance assertions that pin generated implementation internals rather than observable behavior

summary: There is no supported way to launch the product through the Run target to a bounded, asserted outcome, so the exit-0 success path could only be exercised by patching a scratch copy of build.fsx to pass --scene-evidence.

cost: one scratch copy of build.fsx and an extra verification round to prove runInteractive's success path
owner: FS.GG.UI scaffold template — the Run target has no bounded smoke-launch mode; this cycle added FSGG_RUN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS as a partial answer
